question.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the vector $\mathbf{x}$ below, find the value of $x_2,$ the second component of $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}.$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275576/assets/c4e78bff8fa8544adb2d150f1cbe0ebc47370949b8198b1c495c0b0a84147798.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2,\,\mathbf{q}_3.$ 

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275576/assets/0eaf45bf0a651744841124a131304a22353ac85f2ebe5ae12ece10d515656469.svg) where $x_i = \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}{\mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}.$ 

Computing $x_2,$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{2}}{{q}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 1+6\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-4)}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4+6+8}{1+1+16} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
